headline: Funding flows. Space bureaucracy lingers. Debris cleanup begins.
deck: This week highlights funding trends and bureaucratic hurdles in military space.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in a Series C round to enhance its co-orbital security capabilities, a timely boost as the DoD increasingly emphasizes space domain awareness. The company’s valuation now sits at $1.6B, proving that in this market, revenue trumps mere ambition. With the DoD's increasing focus on space, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on upcoming contracts.
stories.soWhat: The military's appetite for space security is growing, and True Anomaly's funding suggests they might be the new go-to for co-orbital solutions.

stories.head: Military space ambitions face bureaucratic hurdles
stories.body: Despite a booming military space sector, bureaucratic delays are hindering progress, as highlighted by recent discussions in Washington. The FY27 budget has earmarked an additional $1.4B for space resilience, yet the path from funding to deployment is still fraught with red tape. This friction could slow down critical advancements in national security capabilities, as agencies scramble to align their priorities.
stories.soWhat: When money meets bureaucracy, the real question is whether the military can turn cash into capability without getting stuck in meetings.

stories.head: Odin Space opens LA office for debris cleanup
stories.body: Odin Space has opened a new office in Los Angeles, targeting the growing problem of sub-centimeter orbital debris. As the space economy expands, so does the need for effective debris management, and Odin aims to position itself as a leader in this niche. The move comes as various stakeholders recognize that cleaning up space is as critical as launching new assets.
stories.soWhat: With debris becoming a pressing issue, Odin's focus on cleanup might just make them the unsung heroes of the next space race.

watchlist.body: As the FY27 budget discussions continue, expect more funding adjustments impacting space resilience and security initiatives.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly contracts
watchlist.body: With their recent funding, True Anomaly is poised to win significant contracts in the co-orbital space domain awareness sector.

watchlist.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could signal deeper issues in defense technology development.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
